passage: A rider's post appeared on Friday evening: the front brake on scooter 214 felt spongy and had nearly failed on a slope. Devika, who runs the scooter-rental firm in Pune, saw it and chose not to reply. 'It'll be buried by the weekend,' she told Ankita from operations. Ankita, uneasy, said that scooter should at least be pulled and checked, and that night marked it 'do not rent' without being asked. Devika still would not answer publicly. By Sunday six more riders had posted their own close calls. On Monday a local news page shared the thread under the line 'The company says nothing.' Phones at the office rang all morning, and Devika finally called an all-hands.

qa.q: Which scooter had the spongy brake?
qa.a: Scooter 214 had the spongy front brake.

qa.q: How did Ankita feel about the silence?
qa.a: Ankita felt uneasy, which is why Ankita marked the scooter 'do not rent' that night without being asked.

qa.q: What could Devika have done differently on Friday?
qa.a: Devika could have replied the same day, thanked the rider, said the scooter was pulled for checking, and named when an update would come.

qa.q: How might riders reading the silence have seen the company?
qa.a: They probably saw a company that did not care about safety, which is why more riders joined in.

grounding: Shows a company staying silent about a real safety complaint, so more users join in and a local matter becomes a wider reputation problem.

'The kettle post has two thousand shares now,' Tanuja said. 'Three more people say the base got hot enough to scorch their counter.'
'We're not responding,' Varun said. 'If we say anything, it looks like we admit it.'
'We haven't said anything for nine days. People think we don't care.'
'It'll fade. These things always fade.'
'It isn't fading. A consumer group has picked it up. And a news website emailed us this morning.'
Varun rubbed his face. 'What are they asking?'
'Whether we've tested it. Whether we'll recall it. Whether anyone's been hurt.'
'Has anyone?'
'One woman burnt her hand. It's in the comments. Nobody from us replied to her.'
Varun was quiet for a long moment. 'Stop all sales today,' he said finally. 'Get the engineers on the base. And write to her first.'

qa.q: How many days had the company said nothing?
Why did Varun want to stay silent at first, and what was he afraid of?
qa.a: He was afraid that any response would look like admitting fault, so silence felt safer.

qa.q: What should the company have done on the first day?
qa.a: Acknowledged the safety complaint publicly, paused sales while testing the base, and contacted the people affected.

qa.q: How might the woman who burnt her hand see the company's silence?
qa.a: She probably felt ignored and angry, since nobody replied even after she was hurt.

grounding: It shows a company staying silent about a real safety complaint, so more users join in and it becomes a wider reputation problem.

I'm Rekha, and I was in the social media team when the helmet complaint came in. A parent posted that the chin strap on our children's cycle helmet snapped the first time her son fell. She added a photo. Our head said, 'Don't engage. It'll draw attention.'
So we didn't. Two more parents posted similar photos. Then a parenting page with a big following shared all three, asking why we were silent. Silence, it turned out, read as 'we don't care about children'. Within a week, two shops returned their stock. Aparna, my colleague, kept saying, 'We could have just said we're checking.'
What finally changed things was a test the quality team ran on their own: the strap failed. That afternoon we paused sales and posted a recall notice. It came three weeks too late for our name.

qa.q: What did the parent say happened to the chin strap?
qa.a: It snapped the first time her son fell.

qa.q: How does Rekha seem to feel looking back?
qa.a: Rekha seems regretful and uncomfortable, aware that the silence made things worse and the recall came late.

qa.q: What could the company have posted on day one?
qa.a: A short reply saying sorry, that the strap was being tested urgently and that parents should stop using the helmet until the result came.

qa.q: How might the parents who posted see the recall?
qa.a: They may feel relieved the helmets were recalled, but angry that it took three weeks and more posts.

grounding: It shows a company staying silent about a real safety complaint until more users join in and a local issue becomes a wider reputation problem.
